Science.name: Cell Biology
Science.definition: Mitochondria generate energy in the form of ATP via aerobic respiration and possess their own distinct circular DNA.
key_facts: This organelle contains inner membrane folds called cristae that maximize surface area for ATP synthase during oxidative phosphorylation. Because it retains its own independent circular DNA and ribosomes, it serves as primary evidence for the endosymbiotic theory. For the point, name this double-membraned organelle commonly nicknamed the powerhouse of the cell.

Science.name: Photosynthesis
Science.definition: Photosynthesis converts solar energy, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose and oxygen inside plant chloroplasts.
key_facts: During the light-independent reactions of this pathway, carbon dioxide fixation is catalyzed by the enzyme RuBisCO within the stroma. This biological process utilizes chlorophyll pigments to absorb solar radiation and splits water molecules to generate oxygen gas alongside glucose. For the point, name this process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy.

Science.name: Thermodynamics
Science.definition: Entropy (denoted by S) quantifies the degree of disorder or randomness within a system, which increases in isolated systems during spontaneous processes.
key_facts: According to Nernst's heat theorem, this thermodynamic state function approaches a constant minimum value as temperature reaches absolute zero. Stated in the second law of thermodynamics, its value in an isolated system always increases during spontaneous processes. For the point, name this measure of disorder or randomness in a physical system, often denoted by the letter S.

Science.name: Periodic Table & Elements
Science.definition: Tungsten (symbol W, atomic number 74) has the highest melting point of all pure metals and was historically used for incandescent light bulb filaments.
key_facts: Denoted historically by the alternative name Wolfram, this transition metal exhibits the highest melting point of all pure non-alloyed metals at over 3,400 degrees Celsius. Due to its exceptional hardness and heat resistance, it was historically used to construct filaments in incandescent light bulbs. For the point, name this chemical element with atomic number 74 and symbol W.

Science.name: Acceleration
Science.definition: Acceleration is the rate at which an object's velocity changes over time, measured in meters per second squared (m/s²).
key_facts: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal form of this vector points directly toward the center of the circular path. According to Newton's second law, multiplying mass by this quantity yields net force, and near Earth's surface its standard gravitational value is roughly 9.81 meters per second squared. For the point, name this physical vector quantity defined as the rate of change of velocity over time.

Science.name: Photosynthesis
Science.definition: Photosynthesis converts light, carbon dioxide, and water into glucose and oxygen gas in plant chloroplasts.
key_facts: During the light-independent reactions of this process, carbon dioxide fixation is catalyzed by the enzyme RuBisCO within the stroma into 3-phosphoglycerate. This biological pathway utilizes chlorophyll pigments to absorb solar radiation and splits water molecules to generate oxygen gas. For the point, name this process by which green plants convert light energy into chemical energy.

Science.name: Velocity
Science.definition: Velocity is a physical vector quantity that measures the rate of change of displacement over time.
key_facts: In fluid dynamics, the terminal value of this vector quantity occurs when drag force equals the gravitational force acting on a falling body. Mathematically defined as the first derivative of position with respect to time, it is distinguished from speed because it accounts for both magnitude and direction. For the point, name this physical vector quantity defined as the rate of change of displacement.

Geography.name: World Capitals & Urban Centers
Geography.definition: Istanbul spans both Europe and Asia across the Bosporus Strait and was historically known as Byzantium and Constantinople.
key_facts: This city's historic core includes the district of Sultanahmet as well as the ancient Byzantine Hippodrome. Located on both sides of the Bosporus Strait, it bridges Europe and Asia and was historically known as Byzantium and Constantinople. For the point, name this most populous city in Turkey.

Geography.name: Deserts & Arid Regions
Geography.definition: Antarctica is geographically classified as the world's largest desert due to extremely low annual precipitation rates.
key_facts: The McMurdo Dry Valleys within this vast region are among the driest places on Earth and feature hyper-saline bodies of water such as Don Juan Pond. Although it holds nearly 70 percent of the world's fresh water within its massive ice sheet, its extremely low annual precipitation classifies it as a desert. For the point, name this southernmost continent.

Geography.name: Islands & Archipelagos
Geography.definition: Madagascar is an island nation off the southeast coast of Africa separated by the Mozambique Channel, famous for endemic wildlife.
key_facts: This island's high central plateau features the Ankaratra volcanic range as well as its capital city of Antananarivo. Separated from the African continent by the Mozambique Channel, it is celebrated for its isolated evolutionary history and endemic species such as lemurs. For the point, name this large island nation located off the southeastern coast of mainland Africa.

Geography.name: Rivers & Lakes
Geography.definition: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland body of water by surface area, bounded by Russia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Azerbaijan.
key_facts: This body of water is fed by major rivers such as the Volga, Ural, and Kura, but lacks any natural outlet, making it an endorheic basin. Classified geologically as the world's largest lake by surface area, it holds significant offshore petroleum fields like Kashagan. For the point, name this landlocked saline sea bordered by Russia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Azerbaijan.

Geography.name: Physical Geography
Geography.definition: The Great Rift Valley is a continuous geological trench formed by tectonic plate divergence running through East Africa.
key_facts: This expansive geographic region includes the hyper-saline Lake Natron and the Danakil Depression, one of the lowest and hottest places on Earth. Formed by the tectonic divergence of the African and Arabian plates, it extends thousands of kilometers southwards from the Middle East to Mozambique. For the point, name this massive continuous trench running through East Africa.

Geography.name: World Capitals & Urban Centers
Geography.definition: Istanbul spans both Europe and Asia across the Bosporus Strait and was historically known as Byzantium and Constantinople.
key_facts: This city's historic district includes the ancient Byzantine Hippodrome and the historic neighborhood surrounding the Hagia Sophia. Located along a major waterway dividing two continents, it was historically known as Byzantium and Constantinople. For the point, name this most populous city in Turkey.

Geography.name: Deserts & Arid Regions
Geography.definition: The Atacama Desert in northern Chile is formed in the rain shadow of the Andes and is Earth's driest non-polar desert.
key_facts: This hyper-arid region hosts the high-altitude ALMA radio telescope array due to its extremely dry atmospheric conditions and clear skies. Created largely by the rain shadow effect of the neighboring Andes Mountains, some weather stations here have recorded zero precipitation for decades. For the point, name this driest non-polar desert in the world, located in northern Chile.

Geography.name: Rivers & Lakes
Geography.definition: The Caspian Sea is an endorheic basin bounded by five nations and is the world's largest lake by surface area.
key_facts: This body of water receives flow from major rivers such as the Volga, Ural, and Kura, but lacks any natural outlets, making it an endorheic basin. It holds significant offshore petroleum reserves such as the Kashagan field and is bounded by five countries including Russia and Iran. For the point, name this landlocked saline body of water, geologically classified as the world's largest lake by surface area.

Geography.name: Mountain Ranges & Volcanoes
Geography.definition: The Alborz range spans northern Iran and includes Mount Damavand, the highest peak in the Middle East.
key_facts: This mountain range isolates the central Iranian plateau from northern maritime humidity coming from the Caspian Sea. Its highest peak is Mount Damavand, an active stratovolcano that forms the highest summit in the entire Middle East. For the point, name this major mountain range located in northern Iran.
